newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy approves Finmeccanica-GEC defence deal.
newsitem.headline: Italy approves Finmeccanica-GEC defence deal.

text.p: Italian state industrial holding Iri said on Thursday it had approved a defence alliance between its unit Finmeccanica and Britain's General Electric Co Plc .

Iri said in a statement the much-rumoured alliance would go ahead. Industry Minister Pierluigi Bersani had said on Wednesday that talks were in progress on a joint venture between Finmeccanica and GEC-Marconi, a unit of the British group.

"The Iri board has examined the content of a preliminary agreement between Finmeccanica and the General Electric Company for broad strategic cooperation in the defence sector, and expressed its approval," the Iri statement said.

It said the deal fitted in with plans to focus on Finmeccanica's core businesses, but gave no further details. Finmeccanica, one of Italy's biggest industrial concerns, with aerospace, defence, transport and energy interests, made a loss of 540.4 billion lire ($318 million) in 1996.
GEC and Finmeccanica signed a memorandum of understanding to explore opportunities for defence collaboration in March.
The two companies said in London on Monday that talks were in progress and proceeding well, but said the purchase of the defence operations of one company by the other was not on the cards.
